rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī frames the exposition from 6:100 to the sūra’s end as a detailed unfolding of its opening call to take God as protector and Creator.
rows.anchor: إلى آخر السورة تفصيل لقوله تعالى في أول السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The splitting of grain and kernels elaborates God’s creation of the heavens and earth, while the surrounding passage rejects assigning Him partners.
rows.anchor: فلما ذكر إبداعه السماوات والأرض بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to eat points back to God as the one who feeds and is not fed.
rows.anchor: وهو يطعم ولا يطعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The images of being brought to life and of guidance continue the opening declaration that the Prophet was commanded to be the first to submit.
rows.anchor: فمن يرد الله أن يهديه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gathering scene and similar passages recall the opening warning that the Prophet fears the punishment of a tremendous day.
rows.anchor: إني أخاف إن عصيت ربي عذاب يوم عظيم

words: وجعلوا لله مما ذرأ من الحرث والأنعام نصيبا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the first exposition closes with the warning that the deniers will know, a second exposition begins with their allotting God a share of crops and livestock.
rows.anchor: ولما انقضى التفصيل عند قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Restating a point in a new style after establishing it with proofs makes it firmer in the soul, especially when the second wording adds clarity and fresh notice.
rows.anchor: كان أثبت في النفس وألصق بالقلب

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazālī argues that Qur’anic repetition is never empty of added benefit; readers should examine what precedes and follows the repeated wording.
rows.anchor: قال الغزالي في أوائل كتاب الجواهر

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazālī reads the Fātiḥa’s repeated mention of mercy as signaling both perfect creation and provision for each world and mercy in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: قال الغزالي في أوائل كتاب الجواهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī associates al-Raḥmān with lordship in the first and second creations, and al-Raḥīm especially with the second creation, preservation, recompense, and special mercy.
rows.anchor: وهي أن الرحمن مشير غلى ما قال من جهة الربوبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning against obeying polytheists means returning to the darkness of error after receiving guidance; this contrast sets up the verse’s question.
rows.anchor: معنى التحذير من طاعة المشركين أنكم إن فعلتم كنتم قد رددتم أنفسكم إلى ظلام الضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dead person is immersed in the waves of disbelief’s darkness, possessing no independent life, as if only inertness or nonexistence remained.
rows.anchor: أي بالغرق في أمواج ظلام الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives life by making faith’s lights shine on the heart; when the heart is sound the whole body is sound, and when it is corrupt the body is corrupt.
rows.anchor: بإشراق أنوار الإيمان على قبله الذي إن صلح صلح الجسد كله

words: وَجَعَلْنَا لَهُۥ نُورًا يَمْشِى بِهِۦ فِى ٱلنَّاسِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light is guidance to every good; walking by it among people makes his deeds, character, and speech perceptible to them.
rows.anchor: أي بالهداية إلى كل خير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī takes the likeness either as an example exposing the represented person’s inner core and heart, or as a description of that person’s state.
rows.anchor: وهو ما ينكشف بوجه الشبه روح لبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The darknesses are ignorance, the desire that grows from ignorance, and disbelief that grows from desire.
rows.anchor: من ظلمة الجهل وظلمة ما ينشأ عنه من الهوى وظلمة ما نشأ عن الهوى من الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If even the ideal likeness is rooted in darkness, the represented person is more deeply rooted in it; he cannot leave while his beautified deeds are dearer than himself and his property.
rows.anchor: وإذا كان المثل الذي هو الأعلى من الممثول في شيء كان الممثول عريقا فيه بطريق الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dead and darkness imagery recalls that only those who hear respond, while the deniers are deaf and dumb in darkness.
rows.anchor: والذين كذبوا بآياتنا صم وبكم في الظلمات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The devils’ whispering to their allies produces blindness by beautifying vile acts.
rows.anchor: إيحاء الشياطين إلى أوليائهم مما يوجب لزوم العمى ليس إلا تزيينا للقبائح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer to the astonishing self-harm of unbelievers is that God has made their deeds attractive to all unbelievers through the disposition formed in them.
rows.anchor: ما كانوا } بما جبلناهم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses paralleled omission: being in darkness is stated first to imply it again, and beautification is stated second to imply it at first.
rows.anchor: أثبت أولا كونه في الظلمات دليلا على تقديره ثانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gathering day is a central, previously veiled subject of the sūra: its opening alludes to it and later passages repeatedly disclose aspects of it.
rows.anchor: فذكر هنا سبحانه بعض أحوال الغافلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gathers every ally and enemy, leaving no one out.
rows.anchor: أي أهل ولايتنا وأهل عداوتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God addresses the jinn through whichever troops He wills to rebuke and humiliate them when they have no power to defend themselves.
rows.anchor: تبكيتا وتوبيخا حين لا يكون لهم مدافعة أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here jinn are hidden, fearsome rebellious devils who gain power over humans and see humans from where humans cannot see them.
rows.anchor: المستترين الموحشين من مردة الشياطين المسلطين على الإنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jinn sought and achieved a multitude of human followers by leading visible, sociable people astray until most became their adherents.
rows.anchor: من إغواء المؤنسين الظاهرين حتى صار أكثرهم أتباعكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse’s paired wording uses paralleled omission: the jinn’s concealment implies human visibility, while human sociability implies the jinn’s eeriness and aversion.
rows.anchor: عبر بما يدل على الستر أولا دلالة على ضده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human allies’ speech is linked to an omitted jinn response, reconstructed from the dialogue elaborated in the following sūra.
rows.anchor: هو عطف على جواب الجن المستتر عن العامل في

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past tense presents the dialogue as certain to occur because it is reported by the One who never breaks His promise.
rows.anchor: وذكره بلفظ الماضي إشارة إلى تحقق وقوعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī relates the exchange to the later followers’ blame of their predecessors in the account of the Fire.
rows.anchor: قالت أخراهم لأولاهم ربنا هؤلاء أضلونا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also compares it with the weak followers’ admission that they had followed the arrogant.
rows.anchor: فقال الضعفاء للذين استكبروا إنا كنا لكم تبعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human allies are people who followed and obeyed the jinn in the misguidance they summoned them to.
rows.anchor: أي الذين تولوهم بالاتباع والطاعة فيما دعوهم إليه من الضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say humans enjoyed the jinn’s claims, while the jinn enjoyed human obedience and the humans’ seeking their protection.
rows.anchor: وهم بنا في طاعتنا لهم وعياذنا بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By invoking the appointed term they shift responsibility to destiny: both groups reached death’s decree and jointly denied this day, so both deserve punishment.
rows.anchor: أحالوا الأمر على القدر فقالوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell is the common home of both groups, and appealing to destiny cannot benefit them.
rows.anchor: أي منزلكم جميعا من غير أن تنفعكم الإحالة على القدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their punishment has no end because they firmly intended to remain in disbelief forever; recompense matches the deed.
rows.anchor: لأن الأعمال بالنية وقد كنتم على عزم ثابت أنكم على هذا الكفر ما بقيتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making the punishment’s duration contingent on divine will affirms that God is not bound by any obligation and that His ownership is complete.
rows.anchor: بين سبحانه أن ملكه ليس كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī says God will not will any end to their punishment; the contingent wording increases their torment by dangling a hope that has no prospect.
rows.anchor: وقد تقرر أنه سبحانه لا يشاء انقطاع شيء من ذلك عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The greatest divine name is used to display majesty and guard the divine station, leaving no one able even to contemplate objection.
rows.anchor: ولما كان القصد في هذه السورة إلى إظهار العظمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because ṭāʿim is indefinite under negation, the preceding statement encompasses every eater, whether from the Muslim community or another community.
rows.anchor: نكرة في سياق النفي , يعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse answers the claim that God prohibited nothing for the Jews and that Israel alone imposed the restrictions on himself.
rows.anchor: تكذيبا لليهود في قولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhū ẓufur covers animals with something like a human finger or claw: camels, predatory beasts, and birds that use their talons.
rows.anchor: على ما هو كالإصبع للآدمي من الإبل والسباع والطيور التي تتقوى بأظفارها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cattle and sheep, which have cloven hooves, were subject to the prohibition on their fats.
rows.anchor: أي التي هي ذوات الأظلاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥawāyā are the coiled, intertwined intestines; Biqāʿī gives ḥawiya as the singular and the pattern faʿāʾil, like safīna and safāʾin, with alternative singular forms.
rows.anchor: وهي الأمعاء التي هي متعاطفة متلوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fat carried on the backs, in the intestines, or mixed with bone is exempt; tail fat is an example, and the phrasing indicates other fats of the two species remained lawful.
rows.anchor: وهذا السياق بتقدم الجار وبناء الكلام عليه يدل على أن ما عدا المذكور من الصنفين حلال لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition of these wholesome foods was a great recompense for the Jews’ transgressions and boundary-crossing.
rows.anchor: التحريم العظيم والجزاء الكبير وهو تحريم الطيبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse’s detail proves the Prophet’s truth: he knew the prior revelation without contact with Jewish followers, study with scholars, or learning from books.
rows.anchor: بيان اطلاعه صلى الله عليه وسلم على تفصيل ما أوحي إلى من تقدمه ولما يشامم أحدا من أتباعهم ولا دارس عالما ولا درس علما قط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The juxtaposition honors this community: necessity can make otherwise forbidden foods lawful and remove hardship, whereas some wholesome foods stayed forbidden to the Jews as punishment.
rows.anchor: تفضيله هذه الأمة بأنه أحل لها الخبائث عند الضرورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison warns this community not to transgress and incur the punishment imposed on earlier people.
rows.anchor: أتم تحذير لهذه الأمة من أن يبغوا فيعاقبوا كما عوقب من قبلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī connects the warning against transgression with the prohibition in 5:1 on hunting while in consecration.
rows.anchor: فبان الصدق وحصحص الحق ولم يبقى لمتعنت كلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s truth is constant from eternity to eternity, as befits His majesty; the proof leaves no room for obstinate objection.
rows.anchor: ثابت صدقنا أزلا وأبدا كما اقتضاه ما لنا من العظمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional wording presents denial as unexpected after the concise revelation that demonstrates the truth so clearly.
rows.anchor: والتعبير بأداة الشك مشير إلى أن الحال يقتضي أن يستبعد أن يقع منهم تكذيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is powerful yet patiently grants the deniers respite until a term known to Him.
rows.anchor: فهو مع اقتداره قضى أنه يحلم عنكم بالإمهال إلى أجل يعلمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When God wills vengeance, no one can repel His force from the criminals.
rows.anchor: نوه بعظيم سطوته فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The criminals are those who sever what ought to be joined; no one should be deceived by God’s delay into persisting in wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: أي القاطعين لما ينبغي وصله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse combines a severe threat with gentle appeal at the highest level of eloquence.
rows.anchor: وفي هذه الآية من شديد التهديد ما لطيف الاستعطاف ما هو مسبوك على الحد الأقصى من البلاغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God predicts the polytheists’ future excuse before they utter it, demonstrating the messengers’ truth and the deniers’ falsehood.
rows.anchor: فقال مخبرا بما سيقولونه قبل وقوعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They argue that if God had not willed their idolatry and prohibitions, He would have prevented them; since He did not, they claim He approves them.
rows.anchor: ولكنه لم يشأ الترك وشاء الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier nations made the same argument: if everything occurs by God’s will, accountability is pointless and the prophets’ claims are false.
rows.anchor: من الأمم الخالية بما أوقعوا من نحو هذه المجادلة في قولهم إذا كان الكل بمشيئة الله كان التكليف عبثا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the earlier deniers tasted punishment, their stubbornness collapsed and they submitted and believed, but belief after seeing the punishment did not benefit them.
rows.anchor: فلم ينفعهم عنادهم عند ذوق البأس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may will an act and punish it because His dominion is complete; He is not questioned about what He does.
rows.anchor: لأن ملكه تام وملكه عام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This passage uses paralleled omission: the first mention of association implies its omission later, and the later mention of denial implies it earlier.
rows.anchor: أثبت أولا الإشراك دليلا على حذفه ثانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although both disputing parties act within God’s will, one must be wrong: a divine command can differ from the divine will.
rows.anchor: لا بد من تضليل إحدى الطائفتين المتعاندتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their claim is at best rhetorical conjecture, whereas foundational theology permits reliance only on decisive proof; the demand for knowledge exposes their ignorance.
rows.anchor: أعلى درجاتها أن يكون من أنواع الخطابة فتفيد الظن في أعظم مسائل علم الأصول الذي لا يحل الاعتماد فيه إلا على القواطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They follow conjecture in their religion’s foundations and sometimes speak by guesswork, sometimes by outright lies.
rows.anchor: تارة بالحزر والتخمين وتارة بالكذب المحض اليقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reciprocal form qāsamahumā conveys extended back-and-forth maneuvering and repeated efforts, with emphatic oath-taking because Adam and Eve were naturally wary of disobedience.
rows.anchor: اقسم لهما لكن ذكر المفاعلة ليدل على أنه حصلت بينهما في ذلك مراوغات ومحاولات بذل فيها الجهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting lakumā implies that Satan assigned all his counsel specifically to them.
rows.anchor: فأفاد تقديم الجار المفهم للاختصاص انه يقول إني خصصكما بجميع نصيحتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī warns against habitual oath-takers: frequent swearing signals a liar accustomed to being disbelieved.
rows.anchor: وان الأغلب ان كل حلاف كذاب فإنه لا يحلف إلا عند ظة ان سامعه لا يصدقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan lowered them from obedience’s height as his own disobedience had brought him down from the abode of honor.
rows.anchor: انزلهما عما كانا فيه من علو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He deceived them by guile and stratagem until Adam forgot his covenant with God.
rows.anchor: بغرور } أي بخداع وحيلة حتى نسى ادم عهد ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ marks the swift consequence, and tasting names the beginning of eating.
rows.anchor: مشير إلى افسراع في الجزاء بالفاء والذوق الذي هو مبدأ الأكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their nakedness appeared and their covering fell away, so each saw what had been hidden from the other; this was the enemy’s aim and they felt shame.
rows.anchor: أي عوراتهما اللاتي يسوءهما ظهورها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yakhsifān means they began sewing leaves together, joining one leaf to another.
rows.anchor: أي يصلان بالخياطة { من ورق الجنة } ورقة إلى آخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their Lord addresses them as their benefactor, the one who had cared for them through command and prohibition.
rows.anchor: أي المحسن إليهما بأمرهما ونهيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī says that they did none of these acts except by God’s permission.
rows.anchor: ولم يفعلا شيئا من ذلك إلا بماى منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question rebukes them for crossing the boundary of what had been permitted; they should have kept away from the tree for their own protection and honor.
rows.anchor: أي أجعل لكما نهاية فيما أذن لكما فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan is the one who arrogantly refused to prostrate, envied Adam, incurred God’s anger, and was expelled from mercy.
rows.anchor: الذي تكبر عن السجود حسدا لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite his evident enmity, Satan plots subtly from every angle; God gave him means to scheme and humans means to escape, commanding them to struggle against him.
rows.anchor: مع ظهور عدواته دقيق المكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One who goes astray follows his worst enemy and abandons his best ally.
rows.anchor: من غوى فإنما هو تابع لأعدى أعدائه تارك لأولى أوليائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam and Eve answer by hastening to repent and confess their wrong.
rows.anchor: فأعربت الآية عن انهما فزعا إلى الا نتصاب بالاعتراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say they harmed themselves by moving from the light of obedience into the darkness of disobedience.
rows.anchor: ضررناها بأن أخرجناها من نور الطاعة إلى ظلام المعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask God to erase the deed and its trace through forgiveness and to raise their degrees through mercy.
rows.anchor: أي تمح ما عملناه عينا وأثرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They promptly confess and magnify their lapse, although it was only leaving the better through forgetfulness, as in 20:115; great people treat even small faults as weighty.
rows.anchor: هو خلاف الولى لأنه بطريق النسيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their immediate confession, unlike Iblīs’s argument, is noble conduct that invites pardon and removes resentment; disputation is base conduct that brings anger and expulsion.
rows.anchor: ولم يجادلا كما فعل إبليس وفي ذلك إشارة إلى أن المبادرة إلى الإقرار بالذنب من فعال الأشراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The descent sends them to the abode of struggle, contest, and conflict.
rows.anchor: أي إلى دار المجاهده والمقارعة والمناكدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam, Eve, and their descendants are enemies of Iblīs and his descendants, while some human offspring will also be enemies to one another.
rows.anchor: أي أنتما ومن ولدتماه أعداء إبليس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no rescue from this conflict except by following the guidance of reason, supported by revelation; the warning calls for constant vigilance even after repentance.
rows.anchor: ولا خلاص إلا باتباع ما منحتكم من هدى العقل وما أنزلت إليكم من تأييده بالنقل وفي ذلك تهديد صادع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth here means the earth as a whole, and mustaqarr is a place of settlement, such as the plains.
rows.anchor: موضع استقرار كالسهول وما شابهها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worldly provision lasts until their lifespans expire and then until the world itself ends.
rows.anchor: انقضاء آجالكم ثم انقضاء أجل الدنيا
